messages:
Kira Volkov: seeing really noisy p99 on the baseline job in `us-east-1` only. p50/p95 are basically stable, but p99 swings 1.6x run-to-run.

Example (Llama-70B chat, shape `S2_streaming_bursty`, H100 pool):
- run 2024-01-24 09:10Z: p99 e2e=5.8s, TTFT p99=1.9s
- run 2024-01-24 10:05Z: p99 e2e=9.4s, TTFT p99=3.3s

`us-west-2` and `eu-central-1` don’t show it. Anyone else looking at this? (threading for hypotheses / next steps)

PerfCanary Bot: Baseline summary diff posted to #perf-canary
- Region: us-east-1
- Workload: S2_streaming_bursty
- Metric: e2e_latency_ms_p99
- Delta vs prev: +62.1%
- Run link: https://grafana.redwood.inference/perf/runs/2024-01-24/09-10Z/us-east-1
(reactions: :warning: x3)

Marcus Reed: +1 noticed it yesterday too. It’s *only* tail. Median decode tpot is flat. My first suspicion is fleet mix drift (different H100 skus or some nodes not on the pinned driver).

Sean Gallagher: if it’s only one region + p99 only, odds are environment drift or noisy neighbor on shared pools. Do we have node-level breakdown / runner metadata captured for those runs?

Kira Volkov: runner metadata is captured but not surfaced well yet. From the raw artifact:
```
region=us-east-1
pool=h100-shared
cuda=12.2
nvidia_driver=535.104.05   <-- this is weird, thought we pinned 535.129
runtime_sha=6d3a9a1
benchmark_lab_sha=3b11c2f
```
The earlier “good” run had `nvidia_driver=535.129.03`.

Vanessa Ortiz: driver mismatch is a smoking gun. us-east-1 had some autoscaled nodes join yesterday from a different image. I can confirm what’s in the pool.

Logan Wright: before we blame driver: are we sure the *measurement* isn’t drifting? We had some TTFT instrumentation edge cases on streaming (first chunk timestamp). If TTFT p99 is moving in the same direction as e2e p99, could be real, but could also be client clock / chunking.

Grace Kim: we can sanity check with server-side counters: queue wait p99, prefill time p99, decode step latency p99. If driver mismatch -> kernel perf should hit p50 too, no? Unless scheduler interacts under burst.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler can amplify tails under burst if a subset of workers is slower (stragglers). You don’t see it on p50 because the fast workers dominate, but p99 catches the slow lane when queues build.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. If some nodes are slower, queue waits become bimodal. Also could be KV cache behavior differences if the pool has a different GPU memory carveout / MIG config.

Yuki Sato: also note: driver changes can affect our autotune cache hits (kernel selection). If autotune re-runs on a subset of hosts, first few minutes can be noisy. Did the job do warmup long enough?

Marcus Reed: warmup is 5 min right now (maybe too short). But the p99 swing persists after the warmup window (I checked the time series panel). Still, driver mismatch + mixed pool explains it cleanly.

Sean Gallagher: action-wise: we should treat this as an env drift incident for the benchmark fleet. There’s an internal ticket brewing for exactly this (INT-1440-ish). Vanessa can you file/update and tag SRE? We need enforcement that the perf runner won’t schedule on nodes not matching the pinned env.

Vanessa Ortiz: yep I’ll update INT-1440 and add details. For us-east-1: I see a split right now.
- ~70% H100 nodes on `535.129.03`
- ~30% on `535.104.05`
Autoscaler pulled in older image.

Kira Volkov: ok that matches. For completeness: why only `us-east-1`? maybe only region with older image still around.

Thomas Baird: if we start tagging nodes w/ driver version as a dimension in metrics, please be careful. That can blow up cardinality. Prefer putting it in run metadata (artifact) and/or a join in the dashboard, not as a high-card metric label.

Logan Wright: +1. For TTFT correctness: I compared server timestamps vs client for the last “bad” run, delta is small (<20ms). So the *measurement* likely isn’t the cause.

Grace Kim: quick experiment suggestion: re-run the exact same workload in us-east-1 but pin to a node selector (driver==535.129.03). If p99 stabilizes, we can close the loop.

Sofia Ivanova: and also do the opposite (force 535.104) just once to quantify the slope. If it’s a real perf difference, we should document it in the variance budget / env pinning ADR.

Yuki Sato: if we do that, also capture kernel selection logs. I want to check if the “slow” nodes are picking different kernels.

Omar El-Sayed: also check scheduler metrics: `queue_wait_ms_p99`, `backpressure_events`, `shed_requests`. If the slow nodes create backpressure, we may see load-shedding spikes that inflate tail.

Marcus Reed: I can kick off two ad-hoc runs from benchmark-lab with node selectors. Will post artifacts here.

Sean Gallagher: please also flag the current baseline dashboards as “suspect” for us-east-1 until we fix fleet. Otherwise people will chase phantom regressions.

Kira Volkov: agree. I’ll add a note in the perf-canary summary + mark the run as env-drift in the run metadata.

Vanessa Ortiz: mitigation plan for fleet:
1) drain old-image nodes from `h100-shared` in us-east-1
2) enforce image/driver in autoscaler config
3) add a preflight check in runner (fail fast if driver/cuda mismatch)

Logan Wright: runner preflight check is good. Also we should store `nvidia-smi -q` snippet in artifacts (driver, vbios, power limit), not just driver string.

Thomas Baird: storing it in artifact JSON is fine; avoid piping the full `-q` into logs (it’s huge). Maybe keep a trimmed version.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: once Marcus posts the pinned run results, we can decide if we need to rerun the last 7 days baselines for us-east-1.

Marcus Reed: ETA ~45 min for the two ad-hoc runs (queue is a bit backed up).

Kira Volkov: cool. Summary of next steps:
- Vanessa: update INT-1440 + start draining old driver nodes from us-east-1 pool
- Marcus: run A/B benchmarks pinned by driver
- Logan: confirm TTFT instrumentation isn’t implicated (seems ok)
- Sean: SRE to add temporary dashboard note + alert suppression for this region/workload until fleet normalized

Will keep thread updated.
